question.problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{0}^{\pi }{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{10}($
{{field-1}} $)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the indefinite integral by  $I=\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that 

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-{e}^{-x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =({e}^{-x})(\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))-\int (\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))(-{e}^{-x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J=\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-{e}^{-x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Then

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =({e}^{-x})(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))-\int (-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))(-{e}^{-x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{1}{3}I.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into our equation for $I,$ we solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}J \\ I & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}(-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{1}{3}I) \\ I & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{1}{9}I \\ 10I & ={e}^{-x}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)) \\ I & =\frac{{e}^{-x}}{10}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =(\frac{{e}^{-x}}{10}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))){|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{-\pi }}{10}(0-(-1)))-(\frac{1}{10}(0-1)) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-\pi }}{10}+\frac{1}{10} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}({e}^{-\pi }+1).\end{aligned}
$$
